rationale: R7 runtime half, the class a corpus-wide name lookup CANNOT see. script/m14/tmp/scala-r7-runtime-probe.ts answers 'is this punctuation-shaped name declared anywhere in the corpus?' and over the full 9,353-file draw it answers YES for every one of the 5,778 punctuation-shaped endpoints — which is CORRECT and useless for this case, because `_` is 'declared' by `val _ = readNameRef()` (src/compiler/scala/tools/nasty/AttributeUnpickler.scala:36, a DISCARDING val that names nothing) and `-`/`+`/`*` are declared as operator methods (Double.scala:149 `def -(x: Byte): Double`). So the instrument that decides this class is scala-placeholder-fragment-probe.ts, which asks whether the endpoint is written as a WHOLE TOKEN where the edge points, and it finds 15 sites over the whole corpus: 9 `uses -> _` from an interpolated `$_` wildcard, and 6 `references -> -` / `-> +` / `-> *` from the Scala 3 PLACEHOLDER type (`val fnMinusPlus1: -_ => +_`, test/files/pos/variant-placeholders-future.scala:7), which the pinned grammar splits into type_identifier('-') + identifier('_') so a type-name walker publishes the operator character on its own. Both name a symbol no source spells. The positive controls are in this same file: an ESCAPED `-_` is a real type alias and must still be published, and an ordinary interpolated identifier must still be a `uses` edge — a guard that cannot tell those from the placeholder is not a guard.

expectRelationships.note: the ESCAPED alias `-_` IS a declared name (quoting is what distinguishes it from the placeholder) and its use must survive the fragment guard
positive control: `s"[$name]"` interpolates an ordinary identifier and must stay a `uses` edge
the over-broad-guard control: `s"[$a]"` interpolates a ONE-CHARACTER parameter, and a guard written as `id.text.length !== 1` drops it

forbidRelationships.note: `val contravariant: -_ => +_` is a PLACEHOLDER (contravariant + inferred), parsed as type_identifier('-') + identifier('_'); publishing `-` names a type no file declares
the covariant half of the same placeholder (`+_`)
`vararg: -_*` — the repeated-parameter placeholder publishes its `*` as a type name
`s"\\*{$_}"` interpolates the WILDCARD; `_` is never a declaration name in any Scala position, so the honest state is absence (R7)
